correctness.rationale: For an interior source the two disjoint slivers of its sentinel gap must each contain a failed edge for a miss; this remains true with one sentinel because the two approaches lead to the same vertex. Inclusion-exclusion gives the recorded gap cost. Its forward second difference at length l is (l+1) times the probability of l specified survivals followed by two specified failures, positive through l=n-m and zero after. Its increments are strictly below 1 for l<L and exactly 1 for l>=L. When n<kL, an unbalanced vector has a shortest gap below L and exchange from a longest to it is strictly improving. When n>=kL a gap below L implies one above L; the analogous exchange improves, and all feasible vectors with gaps at least L tie by the affine tail. Positive integer gaps summing to n are realizable on the cycle. This covers the boundary n=kL, the all-fail case L=1, k=1 or k=n, and connectedness when m<=1. For k>=2 nonbalance in the affine region requires and is possible with at least two surplus edges. Finite checks corroborate, not prove, the general statement.

The sharp onset and exact deficit mechanism test whether an independence-based placement intuition survives a natural finite-budget change of law.
